children: India’s investment banking industry is increasingly becoming a battle for market share rather than market growth.

While deal activity remained robust across equity offerings, debt capital market issuances and mergers and acquisitions, the industry’s overall revenue pool contracted during the first nine months of 2026, intensifying competition for mandates.

According to Dealogic, total investment banking revenues year-to-date in India fell to about $780 million in 2026 from $796 million in 2025, signalling a smaller fee pool despite a healthy pipeline of transactions. In such an environment, gains by one player inevitably came at the expense of another.
The biggest beneficiary of this reshuffle was Citi, which vaulted from fifth place in the 2025 rankings to the top spot in 2026.
The bank nearly doubled its investment banking revenues to $52 million from $29 million a year earlier, lifting its market share from 4 per cent to 7 per cent.

The rise was driven by growing demand from Indian companies for cross-border fundraising and overseas acquisitions. Citi said it helped clients raise nearly $16 billion through equity and debt transactions during the period and advised on about $36 billion worth of M&A deals, underscoring its strength in executing global transactions.

In contrast, some of last year’s leaders lost momentum. JPMorgan, which topped the rankings in 2025, slipped to second place with revenues of $43 million, down sharply from $66 million. Morgan Stanley, the second-largest player last year, also ceded ground and dropped out of the top tier.

Among domestic institutions, Kotak Investment Banking strengthened its position, with revenues rising to $35 million from $32 million. Other local players, including Axis Capital, ICICI Securities, JM Financial and IIFL Capital, maintained a strong presence in the league tables, reflecting the growing ability of Indian firms to compete with global rivals for high-value mandates.

“India’s investment banking market is becoming more competitive. With the revenue pie shrinking, the winners are increasingly those able to secure large-ticket mandates, execute complex cross-border transactions and tap global pools of capital,” said a banker. “In 2026, success was less about riding a rising tide and more about taking a larger slice of a smaller pie,” he said.

title: Smaller Pie, new winners in India’s investment banking
